activity_summary: At the Jackdaw, Ralph Raye brought the Rose news with the dinner. Henslowe has paid seven pounds and two shillings for a throne in the heavens, a chair that comes down out of the roof with a god in it. Yesterday's new play was The Seven Days of the Week, at three pounds ten. You said a glass at four shillings comes down by itself. James Burbage showed the jam with a knife and a crust: the rope will not take a neat turn where it meets the block. Nothing was built, and nobody crossed the river.

entities.name: William Shakespeare
entities.context: Set the four-shilling glass against the chair, and listened to the jam.

entities.name: William Blackwage, Ralph Raye, Richard Hoope
entities.context: Brought both sums from the Rose book, and said he had not seen a jam.

entities.context: Showed the beam, the rope and the jam with a knife and a crust.

entities.name: Richard Burbage
entities.context: Asked what the chair does when the rope sticks, and kept anyone from trying it at the table.

entities.name: Thomas Pope
entities.context: Stayed for the pork, and said a book has not met a rope.

entities.name: Will Kemp
entities.context: Said a chair is a chair until someone sits in it. He did not sit in one.

entities.name: Agnes Tipping
entities.context: Set pork down, and came back for the plates before the talk could finish the dinner.
